## godot-vibe-os
Godot Vibe OS drives the OPEN Godot editor over an authenticated localhost bridge. Work from live scenes, NodePaths, ClassDB, and the source-backed project map.

1. Start with godot_orient({task:"the user's request"}): scenes, selection, import, play, git, and project-map matches in one call.
2. Never guess Godot APIs. Call godot_reflect with an exact className before writing unfamiliar ones.
3. Inspect before you mutate. Scene changes go through godot_get_scene_tree, godot_open_scene, godot_create_node, godot_set_property, godot_reparent_node, godot_instantiate_scene, godot_delete_node, godot_save_scene, which use editor UndoRedo. Do not hand-edit .tscn/.tres.
4. Read before editing text: godot_read_script returns sha256; pass it to godot_apply_text_edits.
5. Verify, then report the exact verdict. godot_verify is an import + GDScript syntax gate, not a test suite; tests stay not_configured unless godot_test_run really ran res://tests/run_tests.gd.
6. For runtime bugs call godot_debug_run; for how the running game moves over time call godot_capture_frames. Editor viewports come from godot_capture_2d_view/godot_capture_3d_view.

ERRORS: GODOT_NOT_CONNECTED means the project is not open with the addon enabled. GODOT_RELOADING is retryable. godot_diagnose_connection explains both.

Resources: godot://project-brain, godot://conventions, godot://action-log, godot://scene-tree.

CURRENT PROJECT MAP (generated, bounded primer)
Project: Catsweeper. Coverage: complete. Project scripts: 3.
Modules: scenes, scripts, shaders, tests.
Use godot_query_project_brain for source-backed details; do not infer facts from this compact primer.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

246	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
247		animation_clock += delta
248		var pointer_ratio := Vector2.ZERO
249		if Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, BASE_SIZE).has_point(pointer_base):
250			pointer_ratio = pointer_base / BASE_SIZE * 2.0 - Vector2.ONE
251		var target_parallax := Vector2(
252			clampf(pointer_ratio.x, -1.0, 1.0),
253			clampf(pointer_ratio.y, -1.0, 1.0)
254		)
255		var follow_amount := 1.0 - exp(-wallpaper_follow_speed * delta)
256		wallpaper_parallax += (target_parallax - wallpaper_parallax) * follow_amount
257		intro_time = minf(intro_time + delta, board_intro_duration)
258		self_modulate = Color(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, _smooth_fade(intro_time / maxf(board_intro_duration, 0.001)))
259		if game_mode == GameMode.PLAYING:
260			elapsed_time += delta
261		else:
262			win_time += delta
263	
264		if pending_cell >= 0:
265			pending_time -= delta
266			if pending_time <= 0.0:
267				var cell := pending_cell
268				pending_cell = -1
269				_toggle_mark(cell)
270	
271		pulse_time = maxf(0.0, pulse_time - delta)
272		error_time = maxf(0.0, error_time - delta)
273		shake_time = maxf(0.0, shake_time - delta)
274		full_board_feedback_time = maxf(0.0, full_board_feedback_time - delta)
275		toast_time = maxf(0.0, toast_time - delta)
276	
277		for key in cat_pops.keys():
278			cat_pops[key] = float(cat_pops[key]) + delta
279			if float(cat_pops[key]) >= cat_pop_duration:
280				cat_pops.erase(key)
281		for key in mark_pops.keys():
282			mark_pops[key] = float(mark_pops[key]) + delta
283			if float(mark_pops[key]) >= mark_pop_duration:
284				mark_pops.erase(key)

286		var particle_index := particles.size() - 1

288			var particle := particles[particle_index]

291				particles.remove_at(particle_index)

301	func _gui_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
302		if event is InputEventMouseMotion:
303			pointer_base = _screen_to_base(event.position)
304			hover_cell = _cell_at(pointer_base)
305			if int(event.button_mask) & MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT and press_cell >= 0:
306				var current_cell := _cell_at(pointer_base)
307				if current_cell >= 0 and current_cell != press_cell:
308					if not drag_active:
309						drag_active = true
310						pending_cell = -1
311						drag_changes.clear()
312						drag_seen.clear()
313						_paint_mark(press_cell)
314					_paint_mark(current_cell)
315			accept_event()
316		elif event is InputEventMouseButton:
317			pointer_base = _screen_to_base(event.position)
318			hover_cell = _cell_at(pointer_base)
319			if event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
320				if event.pressed:
321					if _handle_ui_press(pointer_base):
322						pending_cell = -1
323						accept_event()
324						return
325					_begin_pointer(pointer_base, event.double_click)
326				else:
327					_finish_pointer()
328				accept_event()
329			elif event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT and event.pressed:
330				var cell := _cell_at(pointer_base)
331				if cell >= 0 and game_mode == GameMode.PLAYING:
332					pending_cell = -1
333					_try_place_cat(cell)
334				accept_event()

492	func _validate_full_layout(preferred_cell: int) -> void:
493		var cells_to_check: Array[int] = []
494		if preferred_cell >= 0 and cell_states[preferred_cell] == CellState.CAT and not given_cells.has(preferred_cell):
495			cells_to_check.append(preferred_cell)
496		for cell in range(cell_states.size()):
497			if cell_states[cell] == CellState.CAT and cell != preferred_cell and not given_cells.has(cell):
498				cells_to_check.append(cell)
499		for cell in cells_to_check:
500			var reason := _wrong_reason(cell)
501			if reason.is_empty():
502				continue
503			error_cell = cell
504			error_time = shake_duration
505			shake_time = shake_duration
506			full_board_feedback_time = full_board_feedback_duration
507			toast_text = reason
508			toast_time = 2.4
509			_spawn_error_sparks(_cell_center(cell), true)
510			_play_sound(error_player, randf_range(0.92, 1.02))
511			return
512		_complete_level()

540			return 0.0

547	func _wrong_reason(cell: int) -> String:
548		var row := cell / grid_size
549		var column := cell % grid_size
550		var region := int(puzzle["regions"][cell])
551		for other in range(cell_states.size()):
552			if other == cell or cell_states[other] != CellState.CAT:
553				continue
554			var other_row := other / grid_size
555			var other_column := other % grid_size
556			if abs(other_row - row) <= 1 and abs(other_column - column) <= 1:
557				return "Cats cannot touch, even diagonally."
558			if other_row == row:
559				return "That row already has a cat."
560			if other_column == column:
561				return "That column already has a cat."
562			if int(puzzle["regions"][other]) == region:
563				return "That color already has its cat."
564		return ""

1335		used_columns.fill(false)

1337		used_regions.fill(false)

1345	func _search_solution(row: int, n: int, regions: Array, used_columns: Array[bool], used_regions: Array[bool], columns: Array[int]) -> void:
1346		if validation_solution_count >= 2:
1347			return
1348		if row == n:
1349			validation_solution_count += 1
1350			return
1351		for column in range(n):
1352			var region := int(regions[row * n + column])
1353			if used_columns[column] or used_regions[region]:
1354				continue
1355			if row > 0 and abs(column - columns[row - 1]) <= 1:
1356				continue
1357			used_columns[column] = true
1358			used_regions[region] = true
1359			columns[row] = column
1360			_search_solution(row + 1, n, regions, used_columns, used_regions, columns)
1361			used_columns[column] = false
1362			used_regions[region] = false

extends SceneTree

var failures := 0
var requested_exit_code := 0


func _initialize() -> void:
	_run_deferred()


func _run_deferred() -> void:
	await process_frame
	var packed: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/main.tscn")
	_expect(packed != null, "main scene loads")
	if packed == null:
		_finish()
		return
	var game := packed.instantiate()
	get_root().add_child(game)
	await process_frame
	for player in [game.mark_player, game.place_player, game.error_player, game.win_player]:
		player.stop()
		player.stream = null
	await _run_gameplay_checks(game)
	await process_frame
	await process_frame
	game.free()
	game = null
	packed = null
	await process_frame
	_finish()



func _run_gameplay_checks(game: Node) -> void:
	var saved_unlock: int = game.unlocked_level
	game.unlocked_level = 0
	game._start_level(0)
	_expect(game.grid_size == 5, "first room is 5x5")
	_expect(game._count_solutions(game.puzzle) == 1, "first room has one solution")
	_expect(game._cat_count() == 1, "tutorial starts with one locked cat")
	var wallpaper_sets_valid: bool = game.WALLPAPER_SETS.size() == 3
	for wallpaper_set in game.WALLPAPER_SETS:
		wallpaper_sets_valid = wallpaper_sets_valid and wallpaper_set.size() == 3
		for layer in wallpaper_set:
			wallpaper_sets_valid = wallpaper_sets_valid and layer is Texture2D and layer.get_size().x > 0.0 and layer.get_size().y > 0.0
	_expect(wallpaper_sets_valid, "three complete wallpaper sets are imported")
	for band in [[0, 0], [3, 0], [4, 1], [9, 1], [10, 2], [14, 2]]:
		game.level_index = int(band[0])
		_expect(game._wallpaper_set_index() == int(band[1]), "room %d uses wallpaper set %d" % [int(band[0]) + 1, int(band[1]) + 1])
	game._start_level(0)


	_expect(game.tutorial_step == game.TutorialStep.MARK_SEAT, "first room starts the two-step tutorial")
	_expect(game._tutorial_target_cell() == game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL, "tutorial first highlights its mark seat")
	_expect(game.given_cells.has(game.TUTORIAL_GIVEN_CELL), "tutorial reuses the locked opening cat")
	_expect(game._shares_rule(game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL, game.TUTORIAL_GIVEN_CELL), "tutorial mark seat is visibly impossible")
	_expect(int(game.puzzle["solution"][1]) == game.TUTORIAL_CAT_CELL % game.grid_size, "tutorial cat seat matches the real solution")

	game.intro_time = game.board_intro_duration
	var tutorial_mark_position: Vector2 = game._cell_center(game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL)
	game._begin_pointer(tutorial_mark_position, false)
	_expect(game.pending_cell == game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL and game.cell_states[game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL] == game.CellState.EMPTY, "tutorial single tap waits for double-tap window")
	game._process(game.double_tap_window + 0.01)
	_expect(game.cell_states[game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL] == game.CellState.MARKED and game.tutorial_step == game.TutorialStep.PLACE_CAT, "tutorial single tap marks and advances")
	_expect(game._tutorial_target_cell() == game.TUTORIAL_CAT_CELL, "tutorial then highlights its cat seat")

	var tutorial_cat_position: Vector2 = game._cell_center(game.TUTORIAL_CAT_CELL)
	game._begin_pointer(tutorial_cat_position, false)
	game._begin_pointer(tutorial_cat_position, false)
	_expect(game.cell_states[game.TUTORIAL_CAT_CELL] == game.CellState.CAT and game.tutorial_step == game.TutorialStep.OFF, "tutorial double-tap places the cat and finishes")
	_expect(game.toast_time == game.tutorial_success_duration, "tutorial finishes with praise")

	game._start_level(1)
	_expect(game.tutorial_step == game.TutorialStep.OFF and game._tutorial_target_cell() == -1, "later rooms do not repeat the tutorial")
	game._start_level(0)
	game._paint_mark(game.TUTORIAL_MARK_CELL)
	_expect(game.tutorial_step == game.TutorialStep.PLACE_CAT, "drag marking also advances the tutorial")
	game._start_level(0)

	game.intro_time = 0.0
	var opening_rect: Rect2 = game._animated_board_rect()
	_expect(game._cell_at(opening_rect.position + Vector2(1.0, 1.0)) == 0, "opening board hit-test follows its animation")
	_expect(game._cell_at(game.BOARD_RECT.position + Vector2(1.0, 1.0)) == -1, "hidden opening edge is not interactive")
	game.intro_time = game.board_intro_duration

	var mark_cell := 1
	if game.given_cells.has(mark_cell):
		mark_cell = 2
	game._toggle_mark(mark_cell)
	_expect(game.cell_states[mark_cell] == 1, "single action marks a cell")
	game._undo()
	_expect(game.cell_states[mark_cell] == 0, "undo restores a mark")

	var wrong_row := 1
	var wrong_column: int = (int(game.puzzle["solution"][wrong_row]) + 1) % game.grid_size
	var wrong_cell: int = wrong_row * game.grid_size + wrong_column
	game._try_place_cat(wrong_cell)
	_expect(game.cell_states[wrong_cell] == game.CellState.CAT, "a wrong cat stays seated before the board is full")
	_expect(game.game_mode == game.GameMode.PLAYING and game.unlocked_level == 0, "an incomplete board does not advance")
	game._undo()
	_expect(game.cell_states[wrong_cell] == game.CellState.EMPTY, "undo removes the freely placed cat")

	for row in range(game.grid_size):
		var placement_cell: int = row * game.grid_size + int(game.puzzle["solution"][row])
		if row == wrong_row:
			placement_cell = wrong_cell
		if not game.given_cells.has(placement_cell):
			game._try_place_cat(placement_cell)
	_expect(game.game_mode == game.GameMode.PLAYING, "a full wrong board stays playable")
	_expect(game._cat_count() == game.grid_size and game.unlocked_level == 0, "a full wrong board keeps every cat and does not unlock the next room")
	_expect(game.error_cell >= 0 and not game.toast_text.is_empty(), "a full wrong board explains what to fix")
	_expect(game.full_board_feedback_time > 0.0, "a full wrong board starts playful correction feedback")
	var correction_cell: int = game.error_cell
	_expect(game.cell_states[correction_cell] == game.CellState.CAT, "correction feedback targets a seated cat")
	_expect(not game.given_cells.has(correction_cell), "correction feedback targets a movable cat")
	_expect(game._correction_glow_strength(correction_cell) > 0.0, "correction feedback gives its target a visible glow")
	_expect(game._cat_pose(correction_cell) == game.CatPose.WORRIED, "only the correction target uses its worried pose")
	var full_board_error_particles := 0
	for particle in game.particles:
		if String(particle["kind"]) == "error":
			full_board_error_particles += 1
	_expect(full_board_error_particles >= 18, "a full wrong board creates a strong error burst")
	game._process(game.shake_duration + 0.05)
	_expect(game.error_time == 0.0 and game.full_board_feedback_time > 0.0, "correction card outlasts the short error shake")
	_expect(game._correction_glow_strength(correction_cell) > 0.0, "target glow remains visible after the error shake")
	game._process(game.full_board_feedback_duration)
	_expect(game.full_board_feedback_time == 0.0 and game._correction_glow_strength(correction_cell) > 0.0, "target keeps glowing until it is moved")
	game.queue_redraw()
	await process_frame

	game._try_place_cat(correction_cell)
	_expect(game.cell_states[correction_cell] == game.CellState.EMPTY and game.error_cell == -1 and game._correction_glow_strength(correction_cell) == 0.0, "moving the glowing cat clears its feedback")
	game._try_place_cat(correction_cell)
	_expect(game.cell_states[correction_cell] == game.CellState.CAT, "correction target can be restored")
	game._try_place_cat(wrong_cell)
	_expect(game.full_board_feedback_time == 0.0, "moving the wrong cat clears the correction card")
	var correct_cell: int = wrong_row * game.grid_size + int(game.puzzle["solution"][wrong_row])
	game._try_place_cat(correct_cell)
	_expect(game.game_mode == game.GameMode.WON, "correcting the full board wins the room")
	_expect(game._cat_count() == game.grid_size, "win keeps every cat visible")
	_expect(game.unlocked_level == 1, "win unlocks the next room")
	var win_particle_count := 0
	var left_cannon_seen := false
	var right_cannon_seen := false
	var win_launches_valid := true
	var win_shapes: Dictionary = {}
	for particle in game.particles:
		if String(particle["kind"]) != "win":
			continue
		win_particle_count += 1
		var particle_position: Vector2 = particle["pos"]
		var particle_velocity: Vector2 = particle["vel"]
		if particle_position.x < game.BASE_SIZE.x * 0.5:
			left_cannon_seen = true
			win_launches_valid = win_launches_valid and particle_velocity.x > 0.0
		else:
			right_cannon_seen = true
			win_launches_valid = win_launches_valid and particle_velocity.x < 0.0
		win_launches_valid = win_launches_valid and particle_velocity.y < 0.0
		win_launches_valid = win_launches_valid and float(particle["life"]) == float(particle["max_life"])
		win_shapes[int(particle["shape"])] = true
	_expect(win_particle_count == game.win_confetti_count, "a win launches the configured confetti count")
	_expect(left_cannon_seen and right_cannon_seen and win_launches_valid, "win confetti launches inward from both sides")
	_expect(win_shapes.size() == 3, "win confetti mixes three playful shapes")
	game._process(game.celebration_stagger * 4.0 + game.ui_fade_duration * 0.55)
	game.queue_redraw()
	await process_frame

	for level in game.PuzzleBook.LEVELS:
		_expect(game._count_solutions(level) == 1, "puzzle pack remains uniquely solvable")

	var final_level: int = game.PuzzleBook.LEVELS.size() - 1
	game.level_index = final_level
	game.game_mode = game.GameMode.WON
	game.win_time = 0.55
	game.unlocked_level = final_level
	var modal_point: Vector2 = game.MODAL_BUTTON_RECT.position + game.MODAL_BUTTON_RECT.size * 0.5
	game._handle_ui_press(modal_point)
	_expect(game.level_index == 0 and game.unlocked_level == 0, "play again resets saved progression")

	game.unlocked_level = saved_unlock
	game._save_progress()


func _expect(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	if condition:
		print("PASS: ", label)
	else:
		failures += 1
		push_error("FAIL: " + label)


func _finish() -> void:
	requested_exit_code = 0 if failures == 0 else 1
	if failures == 0:
		print("CATSWEEPER TESTS PASSED")
	else:
		print("CATSWEEPER TESTS FAILED: ", failures)
	call_deferred("_quit_cleanly")


func _quit_cleanly() -> void:
	quit(requested_exit_code)

content.text:
Done. Verify passes and all 83 test checks pass.

**What changed**

*Tutorial* — Room 1 now walks you through the whole board instead of stopping after two taps. It's a list of 5 steps in `catsweeper.gd` (`TUTORIAL_STEPS`): mark one seat, then seat each of the four remaining cats, with a short message per step ("1 / 5", "2 / 5"…). The last step finishes the room, so the win screen is the reward for following the guide. I reused the existing glow-and-prompt drawing — the old two-step code was replaced by the step list, so nothing new was added to the scene.

*Hints* — The footer is now three buttons: UNDO · HINT · RESTART (paw icon). A hint glows the seat you should play next; if a cat is already in the wrong place it glows that cat instead and says "MOVE THE GLOWING CAT". The glow fades on its own. It reuses the tutorial's glow and the existing toast bar. During the tutorial, HINT just re-pulses the current step. New Inspector value: **Hint Highlight Duration** (Feel group, 3.2s default) for how long the hint glow and message stay.

*Title* — "NEKODOKU" in the game header, project name, Android app label, README. I kept the Android package id (`com.strobetano.catsweeper`) so a new APK still installs over Julien's old one instead of appearing twice.

**To see it in the editor:** open `scenes/main.tscn` and press Play. It starts on Room 01 with step 1/5 glowing. Select the root node to find Hint Highlight Duration under Feel.

One heads-up: renaming the project moves the desktop save folder, so desktop progress starts fresh. On Android nothing is lost — the save lives with the app package, which I didn't change.

extends SceneTree

var failures := 0
var requested_exit_code := 0


func _initialize() -> void:
	_run_deferred()


func _run_deferred() -> void:
	await process_frame
	var packed: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/main.tscn")
	_expect(packed != null, "main scene loads")
	if packed == null:
		_finish()
		return
	var game := packed.instantiate()
	get_root().add_child(game)
	await process_frame
	for player in [game.mark_player, game.place_player, game.error_player, game.win_player]:
		player.stop()
		player.stream = null
	await _run_gameplay_checks(game)
	await process_frame
	await process_frame
	game.free()
	game = null
	packed = null
	await process_frame
	_finish()



func _run_gameplay_checks(game: Node) -> void:
	var saved_unlock: int = game.unlocked_level
	game.unlocked_level = 0
	game._start_level(0)
	_expect(game.grid_size == 5, "first room is 5x5")
	_expect(game._count_solutions(game.puzzle) == 1, "first room has one solution")
	_expect(game._cat_count() == 1, "tutorial starts with one locked cat")
	var wallpaper_sets_valid: bool = game.WALLPAPER_SETS.size() == 3
	for wallpaper_set in game.WALLPAPER_SETS:
		wallpaper_sets_valid = wallpaper_sets_valid and wallpaper_set.size() == 3
		for layer in wallpaper_set:
			wallpaper_sets_valid = wallpaper_sets_valid and layer is Texture2D and layer.get_size().x > 0.0 and layer.get_size().y > 0.0
	_expect(wallpaper_sets_valid, "three complete wallpaper sets are imported")
	for band in [[0, 0], [3, 0], [4, 1], [9, 1], [10, 2], [14, 2]]:
		game.level_index = int(band[0])
		_expect(game._wallpaper_set_index() == int(band[1]), "room %d uses wallpaper set %d" % [int(band[0]) + 1, int(band[1]) + 1])

content.text:
Verify passes and all 111 test checks pass, with screenshots confirming English, Japanese and German.

**What changed**

*Tutorial now shows pictures too* — each of the five steps draws its own little image next to the words in the step bar: the X-mark you're about to leave, a happy cat for the first placement, then row lines, column lines, and the colour dots for the rule that step teaches. I reused the rule-card icons already on screen and the existing cat drawing; the only new drawing is the column icon (a mirrored copy of the row one). A test now checks all five steps use different pictures, so it can't quietly become repetitive.

*Seven languages* — English, French, German, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese and Chinese. All the words live in one spreadsheet-style file, `assets/i18n/ui.csv`: one row per line of text, one column per language, so adding or fixing wording is editing a cell. The game picks up the phone's language on first run and remembers your choice after that. A new pill at the bottom right shows the current language with a small globe; tapping it moves to the next one. Japanese and Chinese letters come from the phone's own font, which Godot already falls back to — no extra font shipped.

I moved the difficulty label to the left of that bottom row to make space, and dropped the three rule chips from 30 to 28 pixels so the longer French and Portuguese words fit. The tests now measure every line of text in every language against the box it's drawn in, so nothing can silently overflow — that check is what caught those two.

**To see it in the editor:** press Play. Room 1 opens on step 1 of 5 with a picture beside the text; tap the language pill at the bottom right to flip through all seven languages live.

One heads-up: on a phone with no Chinese or Japanese font installed those two languages would show empty boxes. That's rare, and the only fix would be shipping a large font file, which I didn't add.

Here's what I found about Cat Sudoku mobile games and their rules:

## Overview

Cat Sudoku is a region-based logic puzzle in the same family as Queens and Star Battle, reimagined for cat people. Cat Sudoku keeps the clean row-and-column reasoning but replaces numbers with placement logic, asking "can a cat safely live here without breaking a row, column, region, or touch rule?"

## The Four Rules

The four rules are: one cat in each colored region, one cat in each row, one cat in each column, and no two cats touching — not even diagonally.

## How to Play

You tap once to mark a square with an X — "no cat here, thank you" and tap twice to set a cat down in its spot. Guessing wrong means you lose a heart; three slips and the puzzle resets.

## Game Features

Popular cat Sudoku games include:

- **Catdoku**: Offers 317 hand-tuned levels starting on a 6×6 grid, stretching across 7×7, 8×8, 9×9, 10×10, up to an 11×11 grid. Every board is hand-crafted with exactly one correct solution — no luck, no guessing, just pure deduction.

- **Meowdoku**: Features 150 handcrafted levels, each solver-verified to have exactly one solution.

There is no arithmetic, no trivia, and no guessing required, making these games pure logic puzzles based on deduction.

1. **NeoDoku** - A brain exercise app available on Google Play, though details about this app are limited in the search results.

2. **Ninneko** - An enchanting role-playing game in which players can earn by nurturing Nekos, building lineups to defeat enemies through PvP/PvE battles and campaigns.

3. **Neko Atsume: Kitty Collector** - A mobile cat-collecting game developed by Hit-Point Co, Ltd. for iOS and Android, released on October 20, 2014.

4. **NEKOPARA Sekai Connect** - The latest entry in the popular adventure game series NEKOPARA with various gameplay features.

5. **Doko No Neko** - A walking game that turns your city into a grid of mysterious tiles where you walk in the real world to reveal tiles on the map.

If you're looking for a specific app called "Nekodoku," it's possible it may be a lesser-known app or the search results didn't capture it. Would you like more information about any of these neko-themed games?

content.text:
Answered from the current build (map refreshed, nothing changed on disk).

**1. Are the three rules stated at the start? No.**
Three chips sit at the top of every screen — "1 / COLOR", "1 / LINE", "NO TOUCH" — with small icons. That's a reminder, not an explanation, and nothing at the start says "these are the rules". Worse, there's a mismatch: the chips claim three rules, but the tutorial teaches four things (row, column, colour, no-touch) because "1 / LINE" silently means row *and* column. A first-time player has no way to decode that.

**2. Does the tutorial say why? No — you're right, it just points at the answer.**
The five steps read: "TAP THE GLOW TO RULE IT OUT" · "DOUBLE-TAP THE GLOW TO SEAT A CAT" · "AGAIN · EVERY ROW NEEDS A CAT" · "NEXT · ONE CAT PER COLUMN" · "LAST ONE · ONE CAT PER COLOR". Each names a rule and shows where to tap. None says *why that square* — step 1 never mentions that the square is dead because it touches the sleeping cat. So a player follows the glow, finishes room 1, and arrives at room 2 knowing the taps but not the reasoning.

**3. Copyright: you're safe. Don't change the game.**
Rules and mechanics aren't copyrightable — only the specific expression is (art, text, code, distinctive look). This exact puzzle is decades old (Star Battle / Queens), and the cat version is already a crowded field: Catdoku, Meowdoku, and several browser "Cat Sudoku" games all ship the same four rules *and* the same tap-to-X / double-tap-to-place interaction. When that many titles coexist, no one has a claim on the mechanic. Your art is original, your wording is your own, and I found no app named Nekodoku. Two cheap bits of hygiene: keep "Nekodoku" as the actual app name rather than "Cat Sudoku" (Nikoli holds the Sudoku mark in Japan, and a generic name invites store complaints, which get processed on suspicion rather than merit), and keep every asset home-made. I'm not a lawyer, but there's nothing here worth redesigning around.

**What I'd fix instead — the teaching.** Two small changes, both reusing what's there:
- A one-time "how to play" card before room 1, using the existing feedback-card drawing and the three rule icons, spelling out that a line means row *and* column. Tap to start.
- Rewrite the five tutorial lines to lead with the reason, and reuse the existing rule-pulse to flash the cat that causes it — so step 1 flashes the sleeping cat and says the square touches it. The message bar only fits about 40 characters at the current text size, so the reason and the action would need to alternate in the bar rather than share one line, which means one new timing value in the Inspector.

Want me to build both?

Sources: [Catdoku on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/catdoku-cat-sudoku-puzzle/id6775778251), [Meowdoku on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.oakever.meowdoku&hl=en_US), [Meowdoku rules page](https://www.meowdoku.org/cat-sudoku)

func _run_gameplay_checks(game: Node) -> void:
	var saved_unlock: int = game.unlocked_level
	game.unlocked_level = 0
	game._start_level(0)
	_expect(game.grid_size == 5, "first room is 5x5")
	_expect(game._count_solutions(game.puzzle) == 1, "first room has one solution")
	_expect(game._cat_count() == 1, "tutorial starts with one locked cat")
	var wallpaper_sets_valid: bool = game.WALLPAPER_SETS.size() == 3
	for wallpaper_set in game.WALLPAPER_SETS:
		wallpaper_sets_valid = wallpaper_sets_valid and wallpaper_set.size() == 3
		for layer in wallpaper_set:
			wallpaper_sets_valid = wallpaper_sets_valid and layer is Texture2D and layer.get_size().x > 0.0 and layer.get_size().y > 0.0
	_expect(wallpaper_sets_valid, "three complete wallpaper sets are imported")
	for band in [[0, 0], [3, 0], [4, 1], [9, 1], [10, 2], [14, 2]]:
		game.level_index = int(band[0])
		_expect(game._wallpaper_set_index() == int(band[1]), "room %d uses wallpaper set %d" % [int(band[0]) + 1, int(band[1]) + 1])
	game._start_level(0)


	var mark_step_cell: int = int(game.TUTORIAL_STEPS[0]["cell"])
	_expect(game.tutorial_step == 0, "first room starts the guided tutorial")
	_expect(game._tutorial_target_cell() == mark_step_cell, "tutorial first highlights its mark seat")
	_expect(game.given_cells.has(game.TUTORIAL_GIVEN_CELL), "tutorial reuses the locked opening cat")
	_expect(game._shares_rule(mark_step_cell, game.TUTORIAL_GIVEN_CELL), "tutorial mark seat is visibly impossible")
	var guided_seats := 0
	var tutorial_seats_valid := true
	for step in game.TUTORIAL_STEPS:
		if not bool(step["place_cat"]):
			continue
		guided_seats += 1
		var step_cell: int = int(step["cell"])
		tutorial_seats_valid = tutorial_seats_valid and int(game.puzzle["solution"][step_cell / game.grid_size]) == step_cell % game.grid_size
	_expect(tutorial_seats_valid, "every tutorial cat seat matches the real solution")
	_expect(guided_seats == game.grid_size - game.given_cells.size(), "the tutorial guides every seat the room still needs")
	var step_pictures: Dictionary = {}
	for step in game.TUTORIAL_STEPS:
		step_pictures[String(step["icon"])] = true
	_expect(step_pictures.size() == game.TUTORIAL_STEPS.size(), "every tutorial step shows its own picture")

	game.intro_time = game.board_intro_duration
	game._begin_pointer(game._cell_center(mark_step_cell), false)
	_expect(game.pending_cell == mark_step_cell and game.cell_states[mark_step_cell] == game.CellState.EMPTY, "tutorial single tap waits for double-tap window")
	game._process(game.double_tap_window + 0.01)
	_expect(game.cell_states[mark_step_cell] == game.CellState.MARKED and game.tutorial_step == 1, "tutorial single tap marks and advances")

	for index in range(1, game.TUTORIAL_STEPS.size()):
		var seat_cell: int = int(game.TUTORIAL_STEPS[index]["cell"])
		_expect(game._tutorial_target_cell() == seat_cell, "tutorial highlights step %d" % (index + 1))
		var seat_position: Vector2 = game._cell_center(seat_cell)
		game._begin_pointer(seat_position, false)
		game._begin_pointer(seat_position, false)
		_expect(game.cell_states[seat_cell] == game.CellState.CAT, "tutorial double-tap seats the cat of step %d" % (index + 1))
	_expect(game.tutorial_step == -1, "following every step finishes the tutorial")
	_expect(game.toast_time == game.tutorial_success_duration, "tutorial finishes with praise")
	_expect(game.game_mode == game.GameMode.WON, "the guided tutorial clears the first room")

	game.unlocked_level = 0
	game._start_level(1)
	_expect(game.tutorial_step == -1 and game._tutorial_target_cell() == -1, "later rooms do not repeat the tutorial")

Both fixed. Verify passes and all 119 test checks pass; I watched the card render on screen.

**The rules are now stated up front.** Room 1 opens on a "HOW TO PLAY" card with the sleepy cat, the three rules spelled out in full sentences, and "TAP ANYWHERE TO START". It reuses the three icons already on the rule chips, so the picture on the card and the chip you'll see all game are the same drawing. The middle line reads "One cat in every row and column", which clears up the "1 / LINE" chip you could never decode. The card only appears when the guided room starts, so it never gets in the way later.

**The tutorial now says why before it says what.** Each of the five steps opens by flashing the cat that causes the deduction and printing the reason — "IT SITS NEXT TO THE SLEEPING CAT", "THE NEW CAT CLEARS THIS ROW", "TWO COLUMNS AND A COLOR ARE USED" — then after a couple of seconds the same bar switches to the tap to make. The flash uses the rule-pulse that was already in the game (it lights up the causing cat's row, column, colour and neighbours), so the player sees the blocked squares rather than reading about them. Tapping HINT during the tutorial replays the reason instead of just re-glowing the answer.

Two honest notes. Steps 3, 4 and 5 are genuinely forced — the reason given is the whole proof, and a test checks each step blames a cat that is actually seated by then. Step 2 isn't forced by one move in this puzzle, so it says the sleeping cat blocks the seats around it rather than claiming it's the only option; I didn't want the tutorial teaching a deduction that isn't true. The action lines for steps 3-5 now reuse the hint's own wording, so three duplicate lines came out of the translation file.

All nine new lines are translated into the seven languages, and the width check covers the new card and reason lines too.

**To see it:** press Play. The card comes up first; tap it away and watch the step bar — it shows the reason with the causing cat flashing, then switches to the instruction. New Inspector values under Feel: Tutorial Reason Duration (how long the why stays up, 2.6s) and Rules Card Intro Duration (the card's pop-in, 0.42s).

if game_mode != GameMode.PLAYING or given_cells.has(cell):
		return
	var old_state := cell_states[cell]
	var new_state := CellState.MARKED
	if old_state == CellState.MARKED or old_state == CellState.CAT:
		new_state = CellState.EMPTY
	_push_history_change(cell, old_state)
	cell_states[cell] = new_state
	if old_state == CellState.CAT:
		error_cell = -1
		error_time = 0.0
		shake_time = 0.0
		full_board_feedback_time = 0.0
		toast_time = 0.0
	if new_state == CellState.MARKED:
		mark_pops[cell] = 0.0
		_play_sound(mark_player, randf_range(0.96, 1.06))
	else:
		_play_sound(mark_player, 0.88)
	if new_state == CellState.MARKED:
		_update_tutorial_progress()


func _paint_mark(cell: int) -> void:
	if cell < 0 or cell >= cell_states.size() or given_cells.has(cell) or drag_seen.has(cell):
		return
	drag_seen[cell] = true
	if cell_states[cell] != CellState.EMPTY:
		return
	drag_changes.append({"cell": cell, "state": cell_states[cell]})
	cell_states[cell] = CellState.MARKED
	mark_pops[cell] = 0.0
	_play_sound(mark_player, randf_range(0.94, 1.08))
	_update_tutorial_progress()


func _try_place_cat(cell: int) -> void:
	if game_mode != GameMode.PLAYING or given_cells.has(cell):
		return
	if cell_states[cell] == CellState.CAT:
		_push_history_change(cell, CellState.CAT)
		cell_states[cell] = CellState.EMPTY
		error_cell = -1
		error_time = 0.0
		shake_time = 0.0
		full_board_feedback_time = 0.0
		toast_time = 0.0
		_play_sound(mark_player, 0.84)
		return

	if _cat_count() >= grid_size:
		error_cell = cell
		error_time = shake_duration
		shake_time = shake_duration
		toast_text = tr("TOAST_ALL_SEATED")
		toast_time = 2.4
		_spawn_error_sparks(_cell_center(cell))
		_play_sound(error_player, randf_range(0.92, 1.02))
		return

	var old_state := cell_states[cell]
	_push_history_change(cell, old_state)
	cell_states[cell] = CellState.CAT
	error_cell = -1
	cat_pops[cell] = 0.0
	pulse_cell = cell
	pulse_time = rule_pulse_duration
	_spawn_place_sparkles(_cell_center(cell), region_colors[int(puzzle["regions"][cell]) % region_colors.size()])
	_play_sound(place_player, 0.96 + float(_cat_count()) * 0.035)
	_update_tutorial_progress()
	if _cat_count() == grid_size:
		_validate_full_layout(cell)


func _validate_full_layout(preferred_cell: int) -> void:
	var cells_to_check: Array[int] = []
	if preferred_cell >= 0 and cell_states[preferred_cell] == CellState.CAT and not given_cells.has(preferred_cell):
		cells_to_check.append(preferred_cell)
	for cell in range(cell_states.size()):
		if cell_states[cell] == CellState.CAT and cell != preferred_cell and not given_cells.has(cell):
			cells_to_check.append(cell)
	for cell in cells_to_check:
		var reason := _wrong_reason(cell)
		if reason.is_empty():
			continue
		error_cell = cell
		error_time = shake_duration
		shake_time = shake_duration
		full_board_feedback_time = full_board_feedback_duration
		toast_text = reason

content.text:
Done. Verify passes, all 126 test checks pass, and I watched the highlight on screen before calling it good.

**What happens now when you make a mistake.** The moment you seat a cat that breaks a rule against a cat already on the board, the game shows you the pair instead of waiting for the board to fill up. Both cats get a coral ring, the line they share lights up down its whole length — the whole column, or the whole row — and the bar underneath says which rule broke ("That column already has a cat."). The colour case works the same way: the whole colour patch lights up so you can see both cats sitting in it. For a touching mistake it lights the seats around the cat, which is what that rule is about. After a couple of seconds the line fades, but the wrong cat keeps its gold "move me" glow until you move it, exactly like the end-of-board correction already did.

I reused the existing pieces rather than adding new ones: the rule-checking loop that used to only produce an error sentence now also reports which cat and which rule, and that one result drives both the immediate explanation and the old full-board correction card. The tile tinting, the coral ring style, the gold glow, the worried cat pose and the sentence in the bar were all already there — nothing new was drawn from scratch. The old error-sentence function is gone, replaced by the one that reports the clash, and the three copies of the "clear the error state" block are now one.

**To see it:** press Play, go to any room, and double-tap two cats into the same column. New Inspector value under Feel: Clash Highlight Duration (how long the line stays lit, 2.4 seconds).
